Preprint (arXiv; IEEE template; mentions a 'special-session theme' and a link 'to be inserted on acceptance', venue Not stated)
Microsoft Corporation (all five authors)

Proposes an approach (CommitDistill, open-source prototype mining git history into typed knowledge units with a TF-IDF retriever); secondary: evaluates it in an 'illustrative case study' (RQ1-RQ5) against git log --grep and BM25
CommitDistill, versions CD-v1 (regex-only extraction) and CD-v2 (regex + subject-fallback unit, released default); CD-Hybrid rendering (ablation). Baselines: git log -i --grep, BM25 over raw commits

Knowledge store .knowledge/units.json (plain JSON, committed with the code) of typed units: Facts (constraints), Skills (actionable solutions), Patterns (recurring failure modes), each with id, type, title, content, weight, context and provenance (commit SHA, author, date); 9 regex heuristics. No specification document

Extraction phase (asynchronous post-merge hook: normalise commit text, regex matching, length filter, dedup, store) and retrieval phase (triggered by developer, IDE or LLM agent before acting: TF-IDF with type/prior boosts, silence threshold θ=2.5, top-k)
Store is reviewable through git diff/PR workflows (described as a property, not evaluated); IDE integration with human reading proposed as future work
Full prototype (extraction and retrieval) on real repositories; downstream LLM use only as top-3 units prepended to a prompt (no coding agent)
Not classifiable (repository memory/context layer, no specification); authors do not use SDD terms
Existing code bases: mining history of public repositories; downstream task is time-travel bug-fix file/identifier localisation (no patch generated)

5 repositories, 5,000 most recent commits each (25,000 commits; Section V-B says 2,000 each / 10,000), 1,167 units; 40 dual-annotated units; 36 retrieval queries; 12-query budget benchmark; 15-query calibration set; 40 fixes (RQ4); 200 fixes (RQ5)
psf/requests (Python, HTTP client), pallets/flask (Python, web framework), expressjs/express (JavaScript), redis/redis (C, in-memory database), junit-team/junit5 (Java, test framework)
N/A (no participants); two co-author annotators, adjudication by a third co-author

Automatic: deterministic scripts (released drivers), git history time-travel; LLM-as-judge with GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, paired bootstrap CIs. Manual: two co-author annotators labelling units (4-class rubric), relevance judgement of top-1 results on hand-authored queries

Configurations are retrievers; downstream assistant GPT-4o-mini (no agent). -- Budget-constrained hit-rate at 256 chars (12 queries, Table V): CommitDistill 0.750, BM25 0.333, grep 0.083; unconstrained Hit@10 11/12, 8/12, 1/12. -- Hand-authored queries (6, Table IV): CD top-1 useful 3/6, 0 false positives (silent on 3); grep 1 useful, 5 false positives; BM25 5 useful, 0 false positives (values read from jumbled table). -- RQ4 time-travel (40 fixes, Table VII), Hit@1 / Hit@3 / Hit@10 / MRR: grep 0.125 / 0.200 / 0.300 / 0.168; BM25 0.050 / 0.150 / 0.400 / 0.136; CD-v1 0.000 / 0.025 / 0.025 / 0.009 (does not work); CD-v2 0.075 / 0.250 / 0.450 / 0.177. -- RQ5 downstream, GPT-4o-mini assistant, n=200, mean usefulness 0-2 (Table VIII): control 0.703 (baseline); +CD-v2 0.718 (+0.015, CI [-0.035, +0.065]); +CD-Hybrid 0.720 (+0.018, [-0.035, +0.070]); +BM25 0.733 (+0.030, [-0.022, +0.083]); original 3-arm CD-v1 0.663 (-0.040, [-0.090, +0.010]). Quality: does not work (no detectable lift for any retriever); cost: works (short payloads, fast). Hard half (n=102): lifts CD-v2 +0.123, CD-Hybrid +0.142, BM25 +0.162. -- Precision: 21/40 useful (0.525, CI [0.375, 0.675]), κ=0.633

Subjects: 5 public repositories. Configurations: CommitDistill (CD-v1, CD-v2, CD-Hybrid) vs git log --grep vs BM25; RQ5 adds a no-retrieval control. Held constant: same commit window, top-k, pre-fix time-travel discipline, same assistant model and two judge models, paired design. Acceptance criteria: answer-span substring match; file-locality ground truth (RQ4); LLM judges given ground-truth files/identifiers (RQ5). Repetitions: deterministic single runs; bootstrap resampling. Human intervention: none. Three-arm RQ5 design stated as pre-registered (n=40 pilot, then n=200); four-arm ablation designed post hoc (exploratory)

CommitDistill wins budget-constrained retrieval (0.750 vs 0.333 BM25 at 256 chars) and has shorter payloads; on unconstrained auto-derived queries baselines hit 36/36 vs 31/36 (trivial recall); CD-v2 best on RQ4 Hit@10/MRR, CD-v1 worst; RQ5: no retriever beats control on the mean (all CIs include zero), CD-Hybrid vs BM25 Δ = -0.013 [-0.068, +0.043] (indistinguishable)

Distinguished retrievers on retrieval tasks; RQ5 failed to distinguish conditions (inter-judge κ 0.355, judges rank conditions differently, ρ=0.21). Deterministic and scripted, so repeatable (LLM response cache released). Limitations stated: small query sets, author-curated queries, LLM-judge construct validity, minimal-prompt control unlike production assistants, post hoc four-arm design

Recall limited (lexical, regex keywords); yield depends on commit-message culture; precision only on 40 Python units by co-authors; 36 queries too few; RQ5 judges from one vendor, low κ; no evidence of developer productivity or end-to-end LLM utility; trust threats (commit-prose poisoning, privacy, attribution, adversarial silence circumvention). Future: LLM-assisted extraction, neural re-ranker, controlled maintainer study, IDE integration, production assistant study, held-out replication on a third repository

Many internal inconsistencies: 'three' RQs announced, five listed (p. 5-6); Section V-B says 2,000 commits per subject (10,000 total) while Table II and abstract use 5,000 (25,000); redis yield 185.6 units/kc in Table II vs 329.5 on p. 12-13; p. 12 attributes 8.0 units/kc to flask (Table II: express 8.0, flask 14.6); p. 13 says condition ordering matches between judges while p. 10 says it is not preserved; p. 14 calls RQ5 'null with a slight negative trend for CommitDistill' although CD-v2 Δ is +0.015; char audit refers to an unexplained 'PM' arm. Pre-registration of the three-arm RQ5 claimed, no link or registry. Abstract says source accompanies the paper; p. 14 says link 'to be inserted on acceptance'. Tables IV and VI jumbled by pdftotext; Table IV totals read as CD 3/0, grep 1/5, BM25 5/0. Programming language: Python (tool); subjects Python, JavaScript, C, Java
